item.title: Buying a Luxury Home in Weddington, NC: A Buyer's Guide
item.description:
Weddington has a reputation across Greater Charlotte for spacious homes, generous lots and a countryside feel that's still a short drive from the city. If you're shopping in the luxury price range, it's one of the first places many buyers look. But a high-end home on an acre or more comes with questions that a typical subdivision purchase doesn't. Here's what I walk my buyers through when we tour luxury homes in Weddington.

What makes Weddington different

The town describes itself with the tagline "Rural Living Redefined," and its layout backs that up. According to the Town of Weddington's About page (retrieved November 2026), the town covers about 17 square miles, or roughly 11,000 acres, in Union County, and it "consists almost entirely of single-family homes on lots of one acre or more." Only 27 of those acres are zoned for commercial use, with most shopping and dining clustered in the Town Center near NC 16 and NC 84.

For a luxury buyer, that pattern shapes everything: more space between homes, mature trees, long driveways and room for features like pools, outdoor kitchens, detached garages or workshops. It also means fewer commercial conveniences right next door, so it's worth mapping your regular errands before you fall in love with a property.

Five things to check before you buy

Luxury homes on larger lots reward careful due diligence. These are the items I put at the top of the list:

  • Lot details and boundaries. With an acre or more, it pays to know exactly where the lines are. Review the plat and consider a survey, especially if you're planning a pool, fence, guest house or addition.
  • Water and sewer service. Some properties on larger lots rely on a private well or septic system rather than public utilities. Ask which the home uses, and if it has a septic system, schedule an inspection and confirm the system is sized for the number of bedrooms.
  • HOA and architectural rules. Many Weddington neighborhoods have homeowners associations with architectural review. Read the covenants before you write an offer so you know what's allowed for outbuildings, fencing, exterior changes and landscaping.
  • Zoning and future plans. The town maintains a Unified Development Ordinance that sets lot and building standards by district. If you have plans for the land, check them against the rules for that district early.
  • Systems and upkeep. Larger custom homes often have multiple HVAC zones, irrigation systems, generators and specialty features. A thorough inspection, plus a look at service records, helps you budget for the real cost of ownership.

Financing a higher-priced home

Borrowing costs matter at every price point, and they matter more as loan amounts grow. Freddie Mac's Primary Mortgage Market Survey reported that the 30-year fixed-rate mortgage averaged 7.11% and the 15-year fixed averaged 6.45% as of November 12, 2026. Those are national weekly averages, and your own rate will depend on your loan type, down payment and credit profile.

Many luxury purchases use a jumbo loan, which can have different down payment, reserve and documentation requirements than a conforming loan. Talk with a lender early, get a full pre-approval in hand, and you'll be in a stronger position when the right home comes along. A strong pre-approval also gives sellers confidence in your offer.

Property taxes and town services

Weddington keeps its town tax rate low. The town's About page lists a 2026 town tax rate of 3.5 cents per $100 of valuation. That is in addition to the Union County property tax, so check both when you estimate your monthly costs. On a higher-value home, those numbers add up, and I'm happy to help you pull the figures for any property you're considering.

Schools

Weddington is served by Union County Public Schools. School assignments are based on the home's address and can change over time, so confirm the assigned schools directly with the district for any home you're considering.

How I help luxury buyers

A luxury purchase is personal. Every buyer has a different picture of the right home, whether that's a newer custom build with an open floor plan, a classic brick estate on a wooded lot, or a property with room for a pool and outdoor living space. My job is to understand what matters to you, find homes that fit, including ones that may not be widely advertised, and protect your interests through inspections, negotiation and closing.

I also know the nearby options well. If Weddington's inventory is tight when you're ready to move, neighboring Marvin, Waxhaw and the Ballantyne area of Charlotte offer upscale homes worth comparing side by side.

Frequently asked questions

How big are the lots in Weddington?

According to the Town of Weddington, the town consists almost entirely of single-family homes on lots of one acre or more. Exact lot sizes vary by neighborhood and property, so always check the plat or a survey.

Do Weddington homes have public water and sewer?

It depends on the property. Some homes connect to public utilities, while others use a private well or septic system. Confirm the setup for any home you're considering and include it in your inspection plan.

Is now a good time to buy a luxury home in Weddington?

The right time depends on your goals, your financing and the homes available. A quick conversation about your plans and a look at current listings is the best way to decide.

item.title: Living in Matthews, NC: A Local Guide to Town Life
item.description:
Matthews has a way of surprising people. It sits just southeast of Charlotte in Mecklenburg County, close enough for an easy drive into the city, yet it still feels like a small town with a real main street, a weekly farmers market, and green space woven through its neighborhoods. If you're weighing a move somewhere in the Greater Charlotte area, here's a local look at what day-to-day life in Matthews offers and what to know about its homes.

A historic downtown you can walk

Downtown Matthews is the heart of the town. Its historic streets are lined with locally owned shops, restaurants, and gathering spots, and the scale is walkable rather than built around big parking lots. Longtime landmarks like Renfrow Hardware on North Trade Street sit alongside newer favorites such as Seaboard Brewing and Brakeman's Coffee & Supply. Matthews Station adds more dining in the same compact area.

For homeowners, a lively downtown matters beyond weekend plans. Properties within a short walk or bike ride of shops and restaurants often draw strong interest from buyers who want that convenience, and it's one of the features that sets Matthews apart from purely suburban areas nearby.

The Matthews Community Farmers Market

One of the town's best-known traditions is the Matthews Community Farmers Market downtown. According to American Farmland Trust's farmers market directory, the market runs year-round on Saturday mornings, with a main season from April through November and shorter winter hours from December through March. It's a reliable spot for local produce, baked goods, and plants, and it gives Saturday mornings in Matthews a familiar rhythm. Hours can change, so check the market's current schedule before you go.

Parks, greenways, and time outdoors

Matthews puts a lot of effort into its outdoor spaces, and residents use them year-round.

  • Four Mile Creek Greenway: The Carolina Thread Trail lists the Matthews segment as a paved trail of about two miles, running between trailheads near Matthews Elementary School and Squirrel Lake Park and East John Street. It's popular for walking, running, and biking.
  • Squirrel Lake Park: This park on Pleasant Plains Road has a lake with a dock, a large playground, wooded "fairy trails," and restrooms, and it connects directly to the greenway.
  • Stumptown Park: Right downtown, Stumptown Park hosts outdoor concerts and movie nights during the warmer months, making it a natural community gathering place.

For buyers who value outdoor time, homes with easy access to the greenway or a short walk to one of these parks are worth a close look.

Community events throughout the year

The biggest event on the calendar is the Matthews Alive festival, held every Labor Day weekend. It brings live music, food, and vendors to downtown and draws visitors from across the region. Smaller seasonal events, concerts, and markets fill in the rest of the year, so there's usually something happening close to home.

Getting around

Matthews sits along Independence Boulevard (US-74) with quick access to I-485, which makes it a practical base for reaching uptown Charlotte, Ballantyne, and the rest of Mecklenburg County, as well as Union County towns like Indian Trail, Weddington, and Waxhaw. Commute times vary a lot by route and time of day, so I always suggest buyers test-drive their actual commute during rush hour before committing to a home.

Homes in Matthews

One of the appealing things about Matthews is the variety of housing. Near downtown you'll find older homes with mature trees and established lots. Moving outward, there are traditional brick and siding subdivisions from several decades, many with larger yards. Newer construction and townhome communities add lower-maintenance options. Across Greater Charlotte there are also select luxury properties with custom finishes and generous lots, and nearby areas like Weddington and Marvin offer more estate-style homes if that's your goal.

Because Matthews mixes so many property types, pricing can vary widely from one street to the next. That's why looking at recent comparable sales for the specific kind of home you want matters more than any town-wide average.

Public schools in Matthews are part of Charlotte-Mecklenburg Schools. School assignments are tied to each address and can change, so verify the assigned schools for any specific property directly with the district.

Matthews FAQ

Is Matthews part of Charlotte?

No. Matthews is its own incorporated town with its own government, located in Mecklenburg County just southeast of Charlotte.

Is there a farmers market in Matthews year-round?

Yes. The Matthews Community Farmers Market operates on Saturday mornings throughout the year, with reduced winter hours from December through March.

How do I find out what my Matthews home is worth?

The most accurate way is a pricing review based on recent nearby sales of similar homes. You can request a free home value estimate online, and I'm happy to walk through the details with you.

item.title: Selling Your Waxhaw Home This Winter: A Smart Plan
item.description:
Many Waxhaw homeowners assume the smart move is to wait until spring to sell. Sometimes it is. But winter has real advantages, and with the right plan a November-through-February listing can sell well. Here's how to decide whether a winter sale makes sense for you, and how to prepare if it does.

Photo by Thom Bradley on Burst

Why winter can work in your favor

Fewer homes tend to come on the market in the colder months, so a well-prepared listing has less competition for attention. The buyers who do shop in winter are usually serious: people relocating for work, buyers who missed out on a home in the fall, and anyone who wants to close before a new year or a lease ends. You may see fewer showings, but they're more likely to turn into offers.

Winter also lets you get ahead of the spring rush. If you're buying your next home too, selling first means you can shop in spring knowing exactly what you can spend.

Price for today's rate environment

Mortgage rates shape what buyers can afford, so pricing has to reflect current conditions rather than last year's headlines. According to Freddie Mac's Primary Mortgage Market Survey, the average 30-year fixed rate was 7.11% as of November 12, 2026, up from 6.24% a year earlier. Higher monthly payments make buyers more careful about value.

What that means for you as a seller:

  • Price on recent, truly comparable sales. Base it on homes like yours in your part of Waxhaw that closed recently, not on list prices or what a neighbor sold for two years ago.
  • Get it right the first time. A listing that sits and then takes a price cut can look stale. Pricing correctly from day one usually brings more interest early.
  • Think about concessions. In a higher-rate market, an offer to help with closing costs or a rate buydown can sometimes do more for a buyer than a lower list price. It's worth discussing with your agent.

Prepare your Waxhaw home for winter showings

Buyers notice different things in winter, so put your prep time where it counts.

  • Make it bright. Days are short, so turn on every light before showings, open the blinds, and replace dim or mismatched bulbs with warm, bright ones.
  • Show off comfort. Have your HVAC system serviced and keep the receipt to share with buyers. A warm house feels inviting, and a recent service record answers a common question before it's asked.
  • Tidy the exterior. Clear leaves from gutters, beds, and walkways. Clean the front door and add a seasonal planter. Curb appeal still matters when the trees are bare.
  • Keep holiday décor light. A few tasteful touches are fine, but buyers need to picture the space as their own, so pare things back.
  • Plan your photos. Schedule exterior photography for a bright, clear day. Interior photos taken with good lighting will carry your online listing through the season.

Timing your winter listing

Within the season, timing still matters. Listing in mid-November gives you a few active weeks before the holidays. Late December tends to be quieter, while early January often brings a fresh wave of buyers who made "find a home" one of their New Year's resolutions. Your situation and how your home compares to what's on the market should drive the date, so talk through the options before you pick one.

Let your home's story do the selling

Buyers looking in Waxhaw are often drawn by the town's character: the historic downtown along Main Street, local shops and restaurants, parks and greenways, and easy access to Charlotte and Ballantyne. Point out what makes your property special, such as a renovated kitchen, a screened porch, a large lot, energy-efficient upgrades, or a short drive to downtown. A great listing description and a strong set of photos help your home stand out from the others buyers are scrolling past.

Frequently asked questions

Will my home sell for less in winter?

Not necessarily. The season matters less than how your home is priced and how it looks compared with the competition. A well-prepared, well-priced home can sell well in any month.

Should I wait for mortgage rates to drop before selling?

Nobody can reliably predict rates. If rates fall, more buyers may enter the market at the same time, and more sellers may list too. It usually makes more sense to plan around your own timeline and goals than to try to time the market.

How do I find out what my Waxhaw home is worth?

Start with a free home valuation, then follow up with a detailed review based on recent comparable sales near you and your home's specific features.
